newsitem.title: USA: SEC chair responds to US senator on yield burning.
newsitem.headline: SEC chair responds to US senator on yield burning.

text.p: SEC Chairman Arthur Levitt told a key U.S. Senator on Tuesday that his agency is authorized to return the illegal "yield burning" profits that it recovers from firms in its enforcement actions to the victims of the abuses.
"We do have remedies available, including disgorgement (of illegal profits) for violations of federal securities laws," Levitt said in a two-page letter to U.S. Sen. Charles Grassley, R-Iowa.

"Excessive markups on the sale of securities can violate the antifraud provisions of the federal securities laws," Levitt said, responding to a letter Grassley sent to Attorney General Janet Reno on February 5.

Grassley, a member of the Senate Finance Committee, told Reno he is concerned about alleged overcharges by securities firms that sold government securities to municipal bond issuers in connection with refunding offerings.
"We are aware of various allegations that have been made in this regard," Levitt said.
"Please be assured that these allegations are receiving careful consideration by the Commission in accordance with our enforcement responsibilities under the federal securities laws," Levitt said.
